title: Cottage Pie
subtitle: Braised beef mince under a golden mashed potato topping
excerpt: A deep dish of rich braised beef mince with vegetables in a glossy, savoury sauce, topped with a generous layer of creamy mashed potato and baked until the top is golden-brown and lightly crisped.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cottage pie is one of the foundational British dishes, a meat and potato bake that dates back at least to the late eighteenth century. The name cottage pie is believed to derive from the cottage-dwelling rural poor who could afford only the cheapest cuts of meat (minced or leftover meat) and the staple potato. Shepherd's pie is the lamb version of the same dish; cottage pie uses beef. The distinction in name is relatively recent and became standardised in British usage during the twentieth century. The dish is a reliable family meal that can be made ahead and reheated, and the filling is interchangeable with whatever vegetables are available. The mashed potato topping should be well-seasoned and slightly stiff so that it holds a peaked shape and does not sink into the filling during baking. Dragging a fork across the surface before baking creates ridges that become golden and slightly crisp in the oven.

recipeTools.notes: A deep baking dish, approximately 30 x 20 cm.
A large saucepan for the filling and a separate saucepan for the mash.

content.text: The filling must be properly reduced and thick before topping with the mash: a wet filling will make the base of the mash soggy and the pie will collapse when served. Cook the filling until it is just coating the meat and vegetables with no pooling liquid. The mashed potato should be piped or spooned over in blobs and then smoothed over with a fork rather than pressed down flat: a lighter, rougher surface produces a better-crisped top.

items.preparation: peeled and cut into chunks, for the topping

content.text: Brown the mince in batches in a large saucepan over high heat. Remove each batch as it is done. In the same pan, soften the onion, carrot, and celery in a little oil over medium heat for 8 minutes. Add the garlic, tomato puree, and flour. Cook for 1 minute. Return the mince.

Add the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay. Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes until the sauce is thick and coating. Stir in the peas. Season. Transfer to a baking dish.

Make the mash: boil the potatoes until completely tender. Drain well. Mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth. Season generously. Spoon over the filling and spread to the edges with a fork, creating ridges across the surface.
Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the top is golden-brown. Serve directly from the dish.
